key_insight: PIF-MIONet combines multi-input neural operators with physics-informed learning inside IFENN to predict fluid flow while FEM solves mechanical equilibrium in coupled poroelasticity.
engineering_relevance: Integration with the open-source GEOS simulator offers a path toward efficient poroelastic simulations for complex geometries and industrial-scale multiphysics.
method: Stagger FEM mechanical-equilibrium solves with neural fluid-flow predictions.
Fuse MIONet branch outputs to enable early interaction among input functions.
Combine physics and data losses, with domain decomposition for localized flow phenomena.
evidence_signal: Tests span 2D and 3D domains, variable material properties, time discretizations, and unseen loading histories; for complex cases, physics-and-data training used only 0.1% of the training increments used by pure data-driven training.
watch_item: Industrial-scale speedups and robustness beyond the tested scenarios are not quantified in the abstract.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Fusion-MIONet with IFENN: A Generalized Framework for Coupled Poroelasticity Problems
